newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas soars with cold, Gulf line outage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas soars with cold, Gulf line outage.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices surged early Wednesday but pared gains in late trading, propped up by anticipated cold weather in the Midwest and a line leak in Louisiana, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast buyers crowded the marketplace early, pushing prices into the $2.50s on Transco (Station 65). By the end of trading, prices had eased into the low-$2.30s on most of the pipes.
Tennessee Gas Pipeline reported Tuesday that a leak on a portion of its 500 line in Louisiana would cut about 250 million cubic feet per day of gas flows for up to three days.
The cold moving into the central U.S. also boosted pricing on the Midcontinent pipes as traders reported closing most deals in the high-$2.20s to about $2.30.
The Chicago city-gate market ranged anywhere from the mid-$2.70s early to about $2.60 shortly before nomination deadlines.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to dip to levels 10 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit below normal on Friday and Saturday, increasing heating demand very sharply.

In west Texas, early Permian deals were confirmed done in the mid-teens, but these prices were quickly replaced with $2.30 and higher transactions, indicating a rise of five to 20 cents. Prices were equally higher at Waha in the high-$2.20s to low-$2.30s.
The strengthening Texas market filtered into the southern California pricing as Day 1 gas sold in the low-$2.30s.

Further east, prices on the Appalachian pipes followed the trend of the Gulf market, rising about 10 cents to the $2.50s. At the New York city-gate, sources reported closing deals in the mid-to-high $2.70s.
